title: Phong MAT Shader Resource Usage
summary: Official Derivative article on GPU shader resource limits for MAT rendering, especially per-object light, bone, varying, and uniform pressure in Phong/GLSL-style material workflows.
guidance: Use this article when a material-rendering plan needs to reason about why many lights, shadows, projections, bones, or texture coordinate sets can exceed GPU shader resource limits.
Resource limits are per object: a scene can contain many lights, but each individual object should be constrained with Light Mask when only a subset should affect it.
Use $SYS_GFX_GLSL_MAX_VARYINGS to estimate varying pressure before planning heavy Phong/GLSL MAT lighting or texture-coordinate combinations.
Normal mapping changes how light vectors, spotlight directions, normals, and texture coordinates consume varyings, so treat normal-mapped and non-normal-mapped material plans differently.
When one object needs more lights than a single pass can handle, render the same geometry and camera with different light sets through Render Pass TOP and combine the results with Add TOP.
Uniform pressure includes values constant across the shader execution such as diffuse, specular, emission colors, bone matrices, and light color information.
